title: WASP: Exploiting GPU Pipeline Parallelism with Hardware-Accelerated Automatic Warp Specialization
problem: Current GPU warp specialization requires complex manual programming, is limited to coarse-grained global-to-shared memory transfers, and lacks hardware awareness of pipeline parallelism, preventing effective memory-compute overlap for latency-sensitive applications.
motivation: Improving memory-compute overlap through pipeline parallelism can significantly boost performance for applications in machine learning, HPC, sparse linear algebra, autonomous vehicles, and robotics that are sensitive to memory latency and bandwidth.
method: WASP introduces warp-level register file queues and hardware-accelerated address generation for fine-grained streaming and gather memory access patterns. The system uses explicit warp-to-pipeline-stage naming to make GPU hardware aware of pipeline parallelism, enabling pipeline-aware warp mapping, register allocation, and scheduling. A compiler automatically generates warp-specialized kernels from standard code.
key_novelty: Integration of warp-level register file queues with pipeline-aware GPU scheduling and automatic compiler support to enable fine-grained warp specialization without manual programmer intervention.
contributions: Hardware mechanisms including warp-level register file queues and hardware-accelerated address generation for fine-grained memory access patterns
Pipeline-aware GPU resource management through explicit warp-to-stage naming and scheduling algorithms
End-to-end compiler framework that automatically generates warp-specialized kernels
47% average performance improvement on diverse memory-latency-sensitive applications
primary_theme: Automatic warp specialization for GPU pipeline parallelism
